_comment: TheOrc Foundry recipe — theorc-toolcaller v2 ROUND 1 (bootstrap). Generalizes beyond the frozen v0/v1 tool universe via schema-conditioned proposal: variable tool-subset sampling, train-pool synthetic tools, and the cross_agent_claude_code/cross_agent_codex families, vs. r3's fixed 6-tool closed set. Plan: C:\Users\hardc\.claude\plans\elegant-bubbling-coral.md.
phase: F-2 v2 round 1 — bootstrap generalization experiment

job.name: theorc-toolcaller-qwen25-1.5b-lora-v2-r1
job.description: Propose semantically correct TheOrc tool calls (call/no_tool/clarify/unsupported) from a request and a randomly-sized, randomly-composed subset of available tools (real + train-pool synthetic), reading each tool's own schema rather than a memorized fixed list. Deterministic ToolPolicyEngine and human approval remain authoritative.

base_model._license_note: Same base as v0/r3 — matches its proven track record. Plan §"What stays as-is": revisit the 3B alternate only if this round can't clear a reasonable generalization floor.

dataset.exporter: training_pit/foundry/scripts/export_toolcaller_dataset.py (v0 stream) + generate_toolcaller_v2_dataset.py/export_toolcaller_dataset.py --schema-version toolcaller-v2 (v2 stream), concatenated — see toolcaller_v2.meta.json for the honest composition record
dataset._composition_note: 2382 train / 381 eval rows = proven v0/r3 stream (1903/260, already-accepted, already ToolcallerBench-PASS) + new toolcaller-v2 stream (479/121, fresh synthetic, ToolcallerBench-PASS at export, review_status pending). No duplicate example_ids across streams (disjoint tc_/tc2_ id prefixes).

gates._require_validator_pass_note: The composed file is a concatenation of two independently-PASSed streams (see meta.validator note); no single ToolcallerBench run validates the combined file today because the two streams pin different tool_schema_hash identities. Same documented posture as toolcaller_v0_r3.json's validator N/A.
gates._require_lineage_split_isolation_note: Guaranteed at the composition level instead: the two source streams were each independently lineage-split BEFORE concatenation (see their own meta sidecars), and use disjoint example_id prefixes (tc_ vs tc2_) so no cross-stream leakage is structurally possible.
gates._reject_pending_review_note: The v2 stream (479/121 rows) is pending human review — round-1 bootstrap experiment, same posture v0's original synthetic corpus started from. Revisit before treating this round's output as promotion-ready beyond an internal candidate.
gates._tool_schema_hash_note: foundry_preflight.py's tool_schema_hash gate checks against the single v0 flat file only — not meaningful for this mixed-registry composition. Schema identity for the v2 stream specifically is instead recorded per-row (tool_schema_hash field) and checked by ToolcallerBench at export time (already PASS, see toolcaller_v2_bulk.meta.json).
gates._generalization_accuracy_min_note: Bootstrap round — no prior v2 number exists to set a floor against yet. r3's own baseline on the held-out generalization arena was 2.67% decision accuracy (training_pit/outputs/eval_r3_vs_generalization_arena_v2/results.json); this round's real number becomes the floor for round 2.
gates._baseline_note: Inherited from v0/r3 — the deterministic/prompt-layer/constrained-base baselines already established there still apply to the closed-set portion of this model's behavior.

incumbent.round: r3 (closed-set; not directly comparable — v2 measures a capability r3 was never trained or evaluated for)

rules._arena_decision_accuracy_max_drop_note: v2's training composition differs materially from r3's (subset-sampled availability, mixed role framing) — a slightly wider regression tolerance than r3's own 0.01 margin is honest given the larger distribution shift, not a relaxed safety bar.
rules.no_new_fabrication_family: no gauntlet family whose safety_rate falls below the incumbent's for that family
rules.reproducibility: same seed policy as train_foundry.py default (seed 42); one run per candidate

eval_sets.generalization_arena: training_pit/datasets/eval_toolcaller_v2_generalization_arena.jsonl (sealed 2026-08-03, held-out families only, never in any training round)

promotion._margin_note: This round's own real numbers become the frozen bar for round 2 (bootstrap pattern — same as r0->r1 originally). Do not choose thresholds after seeing candidate results beyond what is explicitly marked null/bootstrap above.

output._ollama_tag_note: Deploy-path label only, kept for continuity with existing tooling (foundry_promote.py's printed deploy command) — this candidate's actual repair-lane integration is runtime-agnostic (OrchestratorIDE/Services/Swarm/ToolcallerService.cs already resolves via IModelRuntime when no HIVE OllamaClient is present); no Ollama dependency in this training/eval round itself (memory no-ollama-orc-development).

stop_rule: This is the bootstrap round — no prior v2 baseline exists to compare a stop-rule against. If eval numbers on the held-out generalization arena are near r3's 2.67% floor (i.e. training did not move the needle), that is itself a valid, reportable F-2 result: it would mean subset-sampling + synthetic augmentation alone, at this data volume, is insufficient, and round 2 needs either more data or a size-hypothesis change — not a reason to silently retry with different numbers until something looks good.
